strengths: Well-motivated framework that coherently addresses two genuine limitations of VLA-based driving: lack of exploration and sparse supervision. The unified approach using world modeling for both dense supervision and exploration signals is conceptually elegant.

Strong empirical results on NAVSIM benchmark (PDMS 93.7 with best-of-N, 90.4 without), achieving state-of-the-art performance with only single-view camera input while competitors use multi-view/multi-sensor setups.

Comprehensive experimental validation with systematic ablation studies (Tables 3-4) demonstrating the contribution of RGB/depth supervision (+2.3 PDMS) and reward components. Figure 3 effectively shows entropy-based novelty captures trajectory diversity better than L2 error.
Technically sound and reproducible: detailed hyperparameters, promised code release, clear two-stage training strategy, and principled architectural choices (omni-attention, MAGVIT-v2 tokenizer).
Practical qualitative validation: Figure 4 demonstrates concrete safety-critical failure corrections (collisions, pedestrian risks, traffic violations) that pure imitation learning fails to resolve.
Sensible safety design: Safety-gated reward (Eq. 7) ensures exploration only on safe, high-performing trajectories, mitigating risk of harmful discovery.
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: Dense world modeling (DriveVLA-W0, UniDrive-WM), uncertainty-based exploration (curiosity-driven RL), and GRPO are all known techniques. The contribution is primarily in their combination rather than fundamental innovation.

Modest RL improvements when best-of-N post-processing is excluded: Stage 1 achieves PDMS 88.5, Stage 2 reaches 90.4 (+1.9 points). Ablation Table 4 reveals image reward contributes only +0.03 points while PDMS reward drives +1.7 points, suggesting the image-based exploration signal provides marginal benefit.

Heavy reliance on post-processing: The headline result (93.7) depends on best-of-N trajectory selection (N=6), which adds ~3.3 PDMS points and is orthogonal to the RL training pipeline. Unclear if this post-processing is applied to baselines for fair comparison.

Weak generalization to open-loop evaluation: On nuScenes, only Stage 1 applied (Stage 2 requires closed-loop metrics). L2 error (0.44m) underperforms OpenDriveVLA (0.33m) and AutoVLA (0.40m), suggesting method benefits from NAVSIM's closed-loop nature and may not generalize well.

Pseudo ground-truth depth: Depth maps from Metric3D pre-trained monocular depth estimation, not actual sensor data. Introduces systematic errors that propagate through supervision and exploration signals. Limited analysis of this dependency's impact on results.

Insufficient world model quantitative evaluation: No metrics (LPIPS, SSIM, FVD) for RGB/depth generation quality. Only qualitative results (Fig. 6) with acknowledged fine-grained detail degradation. Unclear how generation quality impacts exploration signal reliability.

Limited exploration signal analysis: Only one qualitative example (Fig. 3) demonstrating entropy's superiority. Lacking systematic analysis of when/why entropy reliably measures out-of-distribution-ness. No sensitivity analysis for safety threshold δ=0.9 or exploration weight λ=0.5.

Computational efficiency not addressed: Stage 2 requires generating future images for each sampled trajectory (G=8) and computing entropy over all tokens. No timing comparisons or practical deployment cost analysis provided.

Missing failure analysis and robustness discussion: No discussion of failure modes, scenarios where uncertainty-based exploration hurts, or cases where safety-gating fails. Only positive examples presented.

Theoretical justification limited: Connection to exploration literature (curiosity-driven learning, intrinsic motivation) not established. Claim that 'uncertainty reflects distance to entire training distribution' supported by only one example rather than principled analysis.
